chapters.html:
It has been years since Mydeimos, crown prince of Kremnos and chosen Chrysos Heir, has gone through a heat.

In an era of fear and uncertainty the people look to the Chrysos Heirs for salvation, and in doing so often forget that before passing their respective trials and inheriting the power of the Titans they are, in the end, simply human. They eat, they sleep, they laugh, they cry, and, like so many others, they must deal with the inconveniences that come with having a secondary gender. Some of the Heirs, such as Hyacine and Castorice, who were fortunate enough to be born as betas and thus free from dealing with heats or ruts, and Tribios, who lost their secondary gender upon being turned into children too young to present, luckily need not concern themselves with such things. There was also Aglaea, who, upon inheriting the powers of Mnestia, had risen above the mortal concern of being an alpha, though she retained many of the traits of one, her already sharp sense of smell only growing more powerful along with many of her other senses, save for her sight. No longer did she have to deal with going into rut, which was fortunate, because being the leader of the future saviors of Amphoreus left no room for a clouded mind or errors in judgment. 

And then there was Mydei, who had the unfortunate luck of presenting as an omega in Kremnoan society, which valued alphas far more due to their bulkier physiques and aggressive tendencies, two things that are perfect for a people who value strength in combat above all else. However Mydei has never let his secondary gender dictate anything in his life, and from the moment he'd crawled out of the River of Souls as a child he'd fought tooth and nail to grow stronger, to take revenge on the Mad King Eurypon, his very own father who'd cast him into the River of Souls to die. Doing so had not only freed him from the cycle of revenge, but also proven to his people that an omega could conquer, could lead, could be the one to save them from the Black Tide. It's a heavy burden to bear, but bear it he shall, for that is his destiny. He will use the immortal body he'd been cursed with to stem the Black Tide as best he can, paving the way for the Era Nova and ensuring a bright future for all of Amphoreus.

Which is all well and good, but even his immortal body is not free from the curse of going into heat periodically, which is why he's forced to take suppressants to keep his hormones at bay and his mind free from becoming dangerously clouded in the midst of the many life or death (temporary or not) situations he faces on a near daily basis. He cannot afford to be out of commission for a week because his body insists that he be bred, and so he, along with Phainon, an alpha and the only other Chrysos Heir currently among them that's susceptible to losing himself to his instincts, are expected to remain on suppressant pills until they either inherit a Coreflame and transcend such things, or die. Both of them have always been diligent about taking them, at least until everything is turned upside down when two travelers from beyond the sky crash-land on Amphoreus one fateful day. It was a miracle that none of them, even Tribbie, had foreseen, and the fact that they seem willing to help with the Flame-Chase Journey is quite unexpected indeed, but certainly not unwelcome. 

Of course every blessing has some kind of caveat to it in Mydei's experience, and this time it comes in form of him being so completely distracted by the arrival of the Trailblazer and Dan Heng, along with the constant threat of the Black Tide looming in the distance, that he completely forgets to take his suppressants. Something he's unfortunately oblivious to, though he does notice the increase in lingering looks he's been getting during his visits to the markets lately...and the baths...and on the street. He simply chalks it up to some new wave of rumors about either himself or the Kremnoans as a whole, something he and his people have had to contend with ever since arriving in Okhema.

Unfortunately with Phainon off serving as a guide of sorts for the visitors from beyond the sky as they assist him in locating the floating fortress of Castrum Kremnos there's no one around to tell him he's starting to reek of pheromones until it's too late.

Mydei has become so accustomed to not having to deal with such things that he doesn't even realize the telltale symptoms he's experiencing are all pointing towards him being in pre-heat, and so they go either unnoticed or ignored. The sensitivity to smell, the increased appetite, the restlessness, the slight elevation in body temperature, all of it is nothing to the crown prince of Kremnos, who's faced down death itself and emerged victorious many times. It's likely just some minor illness from the change of the winds, or perhaps his immortal body trying to store energy for the next battle. Whatever the case he endures it just like he endures everything else, his mind preoccupied with the fate of his people, along with all of Amphoreus. 

However, it is not something that can be ignored for long, and soon he's summoned to the Chrysos Heir baths to meet with Aglaea for reasons yet unknown to him. Being called to a meeting with the Goldweaver in itself isn't strange, but her specifically requesting that he come alone certainly is, and trying to pry an answer as to why out of Tribbie, who'd been sent to fetch him, ultimately proves futile. 

"Sorry De, Agy didn't tell me the specifics, just that she needed to speak to you alone. Don't worry though, I'm sure whatever it is can't be that bad, or else she would've summoned all of us," Tribbie says with that bright little smile of hers that never fails to reassure others even in the darkest of times. Not that he needs reassurance at the moment, but still, he appreciates the gesture. 

"Right. Tell her I'll be there shortly," he says, and with a nod and a little wave Tribbie is off, able to navigate Okhema much quicker than the rest of them with the blessing of Janus. It's a short walk from his chambers to the baths anyway, the path so familiar to him now that he could navigate it with his eyes closed.

It's Lucid Hour when he arrives at the baths, though it's impossible to tell the difference in the time of day when the Dawn Device shines upon the city all day, every day. There are a few people in the public bathing areas, and once again Mydei turns heads as he passes by them, hushed whispers following in his wake. He pointedly ignores them as he makes his way to the lift up to the Chrysos Heir baths, and when he finally arrives he sees Aglaea waiting for him at the top, arms crossed over her chest as she eyes him critically. It's always a bit unsettling to speak with the Goldweaver one-on-one knowing that her golden threads are everywhere, able to detect even the slightest lie, even if Mydei is never one to shy away from speaking the truth. Her presence is as commanding as ever, and there's not even a ghost of a smile on her lips as she approaches him.

"Thank you for arriving so swiftly, Mydeimos," she says, and Mydei simply nods, crossing his arms over his chest with an expectant look. Aglaea's scent is mostly neutral, which is unusual for an alpha, hints of flowers and some kind of perfume lingering about her that give her an air of sophistication and grace. Mydei doesn't usually pay other people's scents any mind, normally too preoccupied to care, but right now he finds himself crinkling his nose a bit in her presence, his sense of smell definitely having become sharper since last he visited this place. Why he suddenly finds her scent, along with everyone else's in the bathhouse unpleasant he cannot say, but it's probably nothing to worry about.

If Aglaea notices his reaction to her scent she doesn't say as much, instead fixing him with that piercing gaze of hers. "I will not waste your time with small talk. The reason I summoned you here is to inform you that your scent has become incredibly potent lately."

Mydei blinks slowly. Then stares. Then scowls, letting out an indignant huff. "My scent? Are you saying I stink? I just took a bath this morning," he says, though thinking back on it he did do a few hundred push-ups between now and then. Hmm...perhaps another bath is in order after this meeting...

Aglaea, however, shakes her head, her expression turning serious...well, more serious than usual, anyway. "I am not referring to your personal hygiene, Mydei. I mean your pheromones," she says, brows furrowing slightly, and Mydei bristles for some strange reason, as if having his pheromones mentioned at all is some kind of insult. And maybe it is, for someone who does their best to simply pretend that they have no secondary gender at all.

"My pheromones? What about them?" he snaps, the words coming out harsher than intended, but Aglaea doesn't flinch, her expression instead changing to one of concern.

"Have you truly not noticed?" 

Okay, now he's getting annoyed. Aglaea said she wouldn't waste his time, and yet it almost seems like she's trying to lead him to his own conclusion about what she's trying to say, which would be fine, if he wasn't already feeling a little on edge today. "Noticed what?? Speak plainly, Goldweaver," he nearly growls the words, his patience running thin much faster than usual. He respects Aglaea a great deal, and would normally mind his tongue around her, but right now he feels nothing but prickly irritation welling up inside him. Maybe there really is something strange going on with his body...

Aglaea remains unfazed, her gaze is as piercing as ever, though her scent sharpens to something almost musky, typical alpha posturing that Mydei has never been fond of. At least he can trust that Aglaea isn't looking down on him and is simply trying to get his attention, as stubborn as he can be sometimes.

"Mydei...you reek of pre-heat," she says oh so matter-of-factly, and Mydei thinks he must not have heard her right, because there's no way she just said what he thinks she said. 

"What?" 

Aglaea sighs. "I said you smell like you're in pre-heat, Mydeimos."

He scowls. If he were speaking to anyone else he'd assume that they were joking, but Aglaea isn't known to joke about serious matters, and one look at her expression is enough to tell him that she is, in fact, speaking the truth.

...oh. Realization finally dawns on him then, though he's none too pleased about it.

This is not the kind of news I was expecting to hear.

Well. That would certainly explain all the staring and whispering he's been subject to lately, but it's also not possible, because he's been on suppressants ever since he first arrived in Okhema. Perhaps the Goldweaver is simply mistaken? Her sense of smell may have sharpened after becoming a demigod, but it certainly isn't infallible...right?

He huffs, waving a gauntlet-clad hand dismissively. 

"That's not possible. You must be mistaken. I've been taking my suppressants, so whatever you're smelling isn't me," he replies, fully confident that he's right, because there's no way he'd forget something as important as taking his suppressants. It would be incredibly foolish and borderline dangerous to miss a dose in the middle of all this Flame-Chase business, even if he isn't the one set to inherit the Coreflame of Strife as Aglaea had once asked of him. He still has many responsibilities to see to, among them being in fighting form at all times due to the constant threat of the Black Tide, and because of that he's never, not even once since he started taking them, missed a dose of his suppressants. And yet Aglaea looks completely unconvinced by his insistence that he'd never forget such an important thing, and Mydei quickly finds himself wanting to leap off the nearest ledge to escape this conversation. 

"I may no longer be the young alpha I once was, Mydeimos, but I know the scent of an omega in pre-heat when I smell it. I practically raised Cifera, and I know all about the changes that occur before an omega goes into heat. I also know how vulnerable omegas can be during this time, and I do not wish to see you put yourself in danger out of stubbornness, immortal body or not," she says, her voice softening in a way that lets the human side her dissenters like to say she no longer possesses peek through. Mydei has seen it before, but never directed at him, and something about the look of concern she gives him has him bristling, his own scent souring from the turn this conversation has suddenly taken. 

"And I'm telling you that you're wrong, Goldweaver. Save your concern for someone who actually needs it," he snarls, turning to leave and end this conversation, desperately needing to blow off some steam before he says something he'll regret. Aglaea lets out a weary sigh as he starts to walk away from her, and Mydei feels the slightest pang of guilt for blowing her off like this. It's not enough to make him stay though, not when everything suddenly feels like too much all at once. The scents of the bathhouse suddenly feel overpowering in the worst way, and his armor feels far too hot despite how much of his body is exposed. It's awful, and he suddenly needs to get far away from this place, and from the alpha who's telling him things he doesn't want to hear.

"If you won't believe me then I urge you to go and count the pills you have left, Mydeimos. Chrysos Heirs we may be, but we are more than capable of making mistakes," she calls out to him, but he's already riding the lift down to the first floor, gritting his teeth when her words manage to reach his ears anyway. 

How absurd. Count my pills? What a waste of time. If I were going into pre-heat I'd know it.

Or would he? The first and only heat he's ever experienced was when he first presented as an omega, and it had been so sudden that he hadn't had time to prepare in advance. Raging teenage hormones combined with the already unpleasant symptoms of a heat had made it a miserable affair, and he had been incredibly lucky to have people he could trust surrounding him when it happened. Krateros, while in shock that the Crown Prince of Kremnos had presented as an omega, had stepped up to guard his tent as he rode out the misery of his first heat, threatening any who drew near with violence should they even attempt to lay a hand on the prince. The man was, and continues to be, more of a father figure to Mydei than his biological one ever could've been, and he'll be forever grateful for his aid during that trying time. It also meant the world to him that the man had not looked down on him when his second gender had been revealed, and it had given him the confidence to continue proving himself to his people as he grew stronger and stronger each day.

But that was years ago, and he's mostly forgotten how it felt to be in heat due to being on suppressants for so long. As he makes his way to his private chambers he feels a prickle of doubt in his mind that has him scowling again, doubt that maybe, just maybe, Aglaea is right. He shakes his head as if that will rid him of the pesky feeling, and while he should he just ignore the Goldweaver's suggestion to count his pills he ends up going to fetch them from his bedside table anyway, glaring at the bottle as if it's wronged him somehow. 

This is ridiculous. 

He grumbles to himself as he plops down on the edge of the bed and opens the bottle, shaking the little white pills into his palm until it's empty. The date of his last refill is printed clearly on the label, along with the amount of pills in total, and Mydei starts methodically counting them one by one, taking the current date into account. One after another he places them back into the bottle to ensure he doesn't count any twice, and oh...there are...more than he expected. Several more, actually, and the higher the number climbs the more Mydei begins to sweat, because there's just no way he was careless enough to forget to take his suppressants, let alone forget an entire week of them. The numbers clearly aren't lying, but out of pure stubbornness and disbelief he empties the pills back into his palm and counts them again, only to be faced with the same harrowing conclusion.

He's missed a week of suppressants. Somehow, some way, he'd managed to fuck up royally, and his mind races with an intense desperation to come up with a reason why he would do such a thing. His days are far from structured lately but he's always made time to stay fit, eat at least one good meal a day, and take his damned suppressants, so what changed? What could cause such an uproar in his life that he'd forget something so important? He racks his brain for the answer, and it doesn't take him long to realize what's changed lately.

The travelers from beyond the sky. Dan Heng and...Caelus, was it? Those two...

They'd crash-landed on Amphoreus exactly one week ago, turning everything upside down by proving that there really was something beyond the boundless sky, beyond the eternal night that had fallen upon all but Okhema, beyond even Aquila's reach, and needless to say it had been a startling revelation for them all. Phainon had been the one to find them in the Abyss, and he'd also been the one to determine that they were trustworthy enough to lead them back to Okhema. And then there had been the attempt to breach Okhema's gates by Nikador's Titankin, and while it had been easy enough to repel them it was also just one more thing that had distracted him from being diligent about taking his suppressants.

He glares down at the bottle, grip tightening on it until he nearly shatters it in his hand, frustration and anger, mostly at himself, roiling within him. It's far too late for normal suppressants to effectively stave off a heat when it's mere days away, and there are no miracle drugs to stop a heat from happening entirely...right?

An idea strikes him then, a possible solution to his problem, and just like that he's tossing the pills aside and practically sprinting out the door, leaving many a confused passerby in his wake. Were he to stop and think rationally for a moment he might realize that seeing one of the Chrysos Heirs sprinting at full speed through the city streets in the middle of the day might be a cause for alarm for ordinary citizens, but thankfully no widespread panic ensues, only confusion and the occasional curse when Mydei nearly barrels into someone in his haste.

He makes it to his destination in record time, something he'll have to brag to Phainon about later (take that, Deliverer!!), but for now he's a man on a mission, and that mission is to find Hyacine in the Garden of Life, hoping against hope that she hasn't yet departed to head back to the Grove of Epiphany. He doesn't know her well, only that she is the Heir tasked with retrieving Aquila's coreflame, but he has heard tell of her miraculous healing abilities, and that's more than enough reason for him to find her and see if she can somehow fix the mess he's suddenly found himself in.

When he arrives the Garden of Life is bustling with both scholars and chimeras, and once again he attracts unwanted attention, a few of the scholars that had been absorbed in their studies looking up to see just who's suddenly stinking up the place. Some of them (alphas no doubt, judging by the waft of musky scent that suddenly assaults his nose) let their gazes linger far too long, and Mydei feels his skin crawl from it, his own scent souring in response. Normally he'd shoot them a scathing glare that could send even the mightiest warriors fleeing with their tail between their legs, but he has far more pressing matters to attend to, and so he does his best to ignore them for now, glancing around the Garden in search of Hyacine.

She is thankfully easy to spot, her bright candy-colored twin tails standing out amongst the crowd, and Mydei immediately makes a beeline for her, pushing past anyone who happens to be standing in his way. She seems to be caught up in conversation with one of the scholars, a cute little grey and white chimera in her arms, its bright blue eyes looking up at Mydei curiously when he approaches. Mydei can't help but stop and stare at it for a moment, the little critter reminding him of a certain Deliverer.

"..."

"Awoo?" the little chimera chirps up at him, and Mydei is suddenly overcome with the urge to snatch the little guy up and protect and care for it as his own. It's so tiny and cute, just like a pup would be, and Mydei's scent quickly turns softer, warmer, and Kephale above is he really experiencing those kinds of instincts already?? 

Damned hormones. I need to fix this, and fast.

"Lord Mydei?" a soft, feminine voice calls his name, and he's immediately snapped out of his thoughts, glancing up from the little chimera to see Hyacine staring up at him in wide-eyed surprise. Her scent is gentle, soft, and very, very muted due to her being a beta, and it's a welcome change from the wafting stench of the bathhouse. "It's rare to see you here in the Garden of Life. Did you need something?"

Mydei clears his throat, trying to appear casual and like he hadn't just sprinted here and had a motherly moment with a chimera of all things. He nods to her question, shifting awkwardly on his feet. "Yes, actually. I need to speak with you about...a private matter," he says with feigned calmness, eyes pointedly flicking over to the scholar that Hyacine had been speaking with before he'd arrived. He stares at the old man intently, who looks more than a little offended about being interrupted mid-conversation (and probably also at the sudden appearance of a Kremnoan where they don't belong, as so many stuck-up scholars have declared over the years). Luckily Hyacine catches on to the urgency of the situation and politely excuses herself, the scholar turning around to leave in a huff. Good riddance. With that they're left alone in their little corner of the Garden, aside from the little chimera, who's decided that Hyacine's arms are the perfect napping spot. Cute.

"Is everything alright, Lord Mydei? You look flushed. Are you feeling unwell?" Hyacine asks, already switching to caretaker mode, it seems. Something about her presence is soothing, comforting in a way that Mydei didn't know he needed, and finally he lets his guard down a little, breathing a heavy sigh. 

"I wouldn't call it feeling unwell, just...unpleasant," he says, and Hyacine tilts her head questioningly, prompting him to continue, "I..." he glances around them once more, an unusual (for him) sense of paranoia that some eavesdropper is in their midst temporarily overtaking him. When he sees only a few other chimeras frolicking about he finally relaxes again, heaving a weary sigh. He didn't think it would be this difficult to admit it out loud, but he manages to push through the awkward embarrassment and mumbles, "I...think I'm going into pre-heat."

Hyacine blinks once, twice, then lets out a little giggle, and Mydei bristles from it, his scent souring enough for even Hyacine to notice. She quickly seems to realize that he thinks she's laughing at him, and she immediately shakes her head, looking apologetic. "Sorry, I wasn't laughing at you, Lord Mydei, I'm just relieved that it isn't something more serious. You had me worried for a moment there."

Mydei grumbles, crossing his arms over his chest. "I realize this may be normal for others, but I haven't had a heat since I presented, and I have never gone through a true pre-heat," he admits, teeth worrying his bottom lip, and he can't seem to hold Hyacine's gaze at the moment, glancing away as a light dusting of pink settles on his cheeks. He feels so pathetic right now, so foolish for letting anxiety over the unknown creep up inside him when normally he would stamp it down before it even had a chance to manifest. There is no word for "fear" in the Kremnoan language, and Mydei has charged into many a battle without a single trace of it, courageous to the point of recklessness, because what is there to fear when death cannot claim him? He's had to fight since the very day he was born, and no opponent, not even Nikador himself, could make him feel afraid.

But this? The idea of his body betraying him and threatening his clarity of mind? Now that is truly terrifying. The feeling of slowly losing control of himself, no matter how natural it may be for an omega during their cycle, is something he wants to avoid at all costs, and it's what has brought him all the way to the Garden of Life to ask for help. And Hyacine, bless her heart, doesn't turn him away, even though her talents are in high demand all across Amphoreus. Her expression is thoughtful, her bright, twinkling eyes looking up at him in a way that makes him feel heard and not judged, something Mydei greatly appreciates at the moment.

"I see. I understand your concern now, Lord Mydei. I could go over the basics with you, if it would bring you peace of mind. It helps to be informed and prepared for things like this," she says, finally setting the little chimera down on the grass to go join its friends. The little guy doesn't seem keen on playing at the moment though, instead flopping over onto its side on the grass and resuming its nap. Yet another trait that reminds Mydei of Phainon, who could fall asleep just about anywhere. Damn that Deliverer for plaguing his thoughts even when he isn't present. Thankfully Hyacine is patient and understanding, awaiting a response from him with a soft little smile on her face that almost makes him think she knows exactly what he's thinking right now. Hmph. Is he really that predictable?

"I appreciate the offer, but the real reason I came here was to see if you have any sort of medication that can stop my heat altogether. As you're no doubt aware, I cannot afford to be out of commission right now, not when all of Amphoreus is relying on us," he says solemnly, and Hyacine gives him a empathetic look, knowing the pressure of being a Chrysos Heir far too well. She also looks like she's hesitating though, fidgeting a little with the pegasus charm on her hip.

"I understand, believe me I do, but...I'm afraid there is no such miracle drug," she says, and Mydei feels his heart drop, the small glimmer of hope that had carried him here instantly snuffed out like a candle in the wind. His frown deepens, and Hyacine looks up at him apologetically, but then a look of consideration crosses her face that has Mydei quirking a brow questioningly. "At least...not one that's been tested and approved for use by the general public," she adds, eyes darting around as if afraid she might be overheard. A bit foolish, perhaps, when Aglaea's golden threads are literally everywhere in Okhema, but hopefully the Goldweaver has more important things to be eavesdropping on than their conversation. 

That tiny glimmer of hope ignites yet again, even if Hyacine's sudden hesitation to say more speaks volumes about the potential dangers of ingesting untested drugs. He looks at her imploringly, hanging on to the possibility of a solution to his looming problem, even if it may not be the wisest course of action. "Then there may be hope," he says, and Hyacine suddenly looks like she's been put under a spotlight, regret clear as day on her face.

"I...suppose, but there's no telling what kind of side effects such drugs could have, even on an immortal body like yours," she says, trying so hard to backpedal that Mydei feels a little guilty about pressing her, but desperate times call for desperate measures. "Plus, I've seen so many patients suffer from taking street suppressants that I simply cannot condone their use."

"I can't die, so I'm-"

Hyacine promptly cuts him off, putting her foot down on the matter.

"Lord Mydei please, forget I said anything! It was a thoughtless comment! I don't want to be responsible for you ending up sick or injured, immortal or not," she says, her expression desperate, pleading. "It's far safer for you to just go through your heat! In fact I have an herbal tea that's perfect for soothing some of the symptoms of a heat, as well as medicine to help you sleep. You're even welcome to stay in one of the clinic rooms until it passes! That way if you need anything I'll be right there to help!"

Mydei feels like the biggest idiot on Amphoreus for getting his hopes up like that, though he can't bring himself to be angry with Hyacine for unintentionally giving him false hope. The poor girl has no doubt seen it all when it comes to caring for patients, and it would be cruel of him to burden her with any potential issues he might have from being careless enough to ingest something off the street. He may not be able to die, but that doesn't mean he can't suffer immensely from whatever potential side effects they could have on him. He is, after all, only human.

He sighs, rubbing the back of his neck as he contemplates what to say, though when it causes a jolt of sensation to shoot through him from head to toe he curses in Kremnoan, because of course his nape would be sensitive right before a heat. Hyacine gives him an apologetic look, crossing her arms over her chest.

"I'm sorry you're going through this, Lord Mydei. There is one other solution that could at least shorten the duration of your heat, if you're willing to hear it."

He feels like he's going insane with the way he instantly perks back up at those words, though he tries not to get his hopes up too much, lest he be disappointed once again. "What is it? Tell me," he says a little more forcefully than he means to, but Hyacine doesn't seem bothered by it, nodding.

"You could always find an alpha you trust to help you through your heat. She seems to take pity on him though, continuing, "but I can tell you that Lord Mydei could use your support right now, even if he might not admit it out loud."

That has Phainon perking up a little, tilting his head like a confused puppy. "My support? He always has that. If something is bothering him then I'll help however I can. The problem is getting him to let me," Phainon says with a pout, and Hyacine nods, giving him a sympathetic look.

"I know, Lord Phainon, and I'm sure he appreciates that. But you also have to realize that Lord Mydei is a proud man from a proud culture, and an omega on top of that. Accepting help might not be as easy for him because it's seen as something Kremnoans just don't do, and showing any kind of weakness as an omega, even if it truly isn't a weakness to ask others for help, could potentially put him in a tough situation with his countrymen. His people look up to him, but that also means that they're constantly analyzing his every move, and being an omega unfortunately means that he's under even more scrutiny than an alpha in his position would be," Hyacine says solemnly. She seems to sense Phainon's racing thoughts as he processes her words, and she reaches over to gently rest her hand on his arm with a reassuring smile. "But that doesn't mean you can't try anyway. It shouldn't take him long to recover, and then maybe you can see about talking with him privately to see if he'll open up to you."

Phainon lets her words sink in as he glances down at the hand on his arm, eventually returning Hyacine's smile with one of his own, this one warm and genuine. He nods, his mind made up on what he needs to do next. "Yeah, you're right. I'll talk to him once he's awake. Thanks Hyacine," he says, and she beams at him, clearly pleased that he's cheered up a little. Phainon doesn't think he's ever met such a kindhearted person in his life, aside from Cyrene. "Ever think about becoming a therapist as a side job?" 

Hyacine giggles at that, a light, bubbly sound that practically radiates rainbows and sunshine. "Actually, I already include that with my other services to those who need it. If there's anything I've learned during my time away from the Grove it's that we Chrysos Heirs can do more than simply protect the people from the Black Tide. We can also help them heal, both physically and mentally." She takes a sip of her tea as she lets her words hang in the air, and Phainon couldn't agree more, really. There's far more to ensuring a bright future for humanity than the ability to fight and defend the people, and Hyacine, Aglaea and Anaxa are all prime examples of that, capable enough in battle but also able to aid humanity with both knowledge and wisdom. He envies them sometimes, since he himself can't claim to be a healer or a leader or a scholar, but as the Deliverer he bears the burden of humanity's hope, and he swears on his life that he will usher in the New Dawn, even if it costs him his life. 

"Yeah, you're right. As usual," he says with a light, airy laugh. "I'll keep that in mind."

Such solemn thoughts can be pushed aside for now though, and Phainon finally takes a sip of his own tea, the hot liquid having a soothing effect on him almost immediately. The floral scent is just subtle enough to not assault his sensitive nose like some flowery scents can, which he appreciates. The hand on his arm eventually withdraws, and Hyacine's smile fades a little as she pulls away, that serious, clinical look she gets when she enters doctor mode soon replacing it. Phainon tilts his head questioningly, unsure why there's been a sudden shift in her mood, and Hyacine lets out an exasperated sigh as she scoots her chair back to get a better look at him.

"You're shivering, Lord Phainon. Are your clothes still damp from the bath?" 

Phainon blinks. He hadn't even realized he's been shivering ever since they made it to the break room, his damp clothing clinging to his skin, and he frowns as he glances down at his lower half, his pants and part of his coat indeed still soaked from the bath. He rubs the back of his neck sheepishly as Hyacine eyes him, feeling a little guilty for making her worry about him too. "Ah...I guess they are, yeah. I didn't really have time to change on my way here," he admits, staring into the depths of his mug as he pointedly avoids her gaze. He'd rather not be fussed over, because he's not the one in the hospital bed right now, but knowing Hyacine she won't drop the matter so easily.

"I understand. However, I would never forgive myself if I let you catch pneumonia from running around my clinic in wet clothes," Hyacine says, and Phainon opens his mouth to protest, but she's clearly not having it. "Once you finish your tea I want you to go home and change and eat something. Neglecting your own health won't help Lord Mydei recover any faster," she scolds him like one would a child, and while leaving the clinic is the last thing he wants to do right now he knows there's no talking his way out of this. Hyacine takes her duties very seriously, and once she's given orders regarding her patient's health she cannot be swayed from her decision. Phainon sighs heavily, shoulders slumping as he reluctantly gives in to her request.

"Alright, alright. I'll go change and eat something, but I'm coming right back here afterwards!" he declares, and Hyacine nods, looking satisfied with that answer. With that decided they continue to chat over tea until it's time for Hyacine to go check Mydei's vitals again, and while the temptation to follow her is strong he knows that'll only get him shooed out of the room again, if not the clinic itself. And so he forces himself to walk past the exam room and out the front door, lost in thought as he makes his way back to his room at the Chrysos Heir villa. Most of his clothes are there, the room he's been staying at in the bathhouse lately more like a fancy lounge than anything, not nearly as roomy and luxurious as the suite Mydei had claimed for himself, the jerk. He can't help but smile as he remembers the argument they'd gotten into over who gets the bigger room, which had been settled over an arm wrestling match that he'd absolutely lost. Of course he doesn't actually mind that Mydei had gotten the bigger room in the end, because as long as he's able to be near the omega he's happy. 

If only he could be by his side right now, where he belongs.

I miss his scent.

It's a thought that comes unbidden, his cheeks warming as he recalls the unique scent of pomegranate and amber that lingers around the omega, hints of sweet honey coming through every now and then that make Phainon want to bury his face in the man's neck and inhale deeply until the scent is permanently burned into his lungs. Oh, how he'd love to rub on his scent glands and cover himself in those sweet pheromones while leaving traces of his own scent on Mydei in return. The thought of it pleases his stupid alpha brain greatly, so much so that he lets his thoughts get carried away, imagining mouthing at Mydei's mating gland and tasting him on his tongue. It has him salivating a little, his cock giving an interested throb beneath the dampened layers of his clothing, and when he finally realizes that he's fantasizing about his best friend in public while he's currently in the hospital he considers tossing himself into the nearest fountain to let the icy cold water shock his system back to sense.

This is exactly the kind of thing that earns alphas a bad reputation. Mydei doesn't need me sniffing after him like some kind of animal, especially not right now.

The barrage of self-flagellation continues until he's back home, and once he's there he quickly changes out of his damp clothing and slips on a simple white button-up shirt and his usual dark grey pants, along with some fresh, dry underwear. He's never going into the baths fully clothed again, not even if Mydei challenges him to another heat tolerance competition. In fact he thinks he'll keep away from the hot baths altogether, not wanting another incident to occur. Whether he can convince Mydei to do the same remains to be seen. 

After he's dressed he goes into the small kitchenette and scrounges up some dried meat he'd cured himself a while back, not bothering with a full meal when he's not even that hungry to begin with. Hyacine only told him to eat something, after all, and cured meat is definitely something. He doesn't linger for long after snacking, ready to get back to the clinic and wait for Mydei to wake up. Knowing him he won't be happy to be questioned about everything that's transpired today, but Phainon is determined to pry the truth out of him, one way or another. If Mydei ends up angry at him afterwards he can accept that, as long as he figures out what's truly wrong with his best friend. Only then can he possibly hope to help, even if Mydei might not easily accept it.

If he wasn't infuriatingly stubborn he wouldn't be Mydei.

The same could be said of him as well, but that's neither here nor there. With that he heads back out of the villa, taking a shortcut through the markets, where vendors are preparing to close up shop for the day. He passes by a man selling candied fruits and other confectionery, and it gives him the idea of bringing Mydei a gift, something he can actually make use of while he's recovering to restore his depleted energy. The man is quite fond of sweets, so it's really a no-brainer, and Phainon fishes a few coins out of his pockets, thankful that he'd forgotten to empty them the last time he washed these pants. It's just barely enough to cover the cost of the assorted mix of candies, and the vendor places them in a decorative red and gold box that Phainon thinks Mydei will like, given his fondness for all things red. The vendor then wraps it up with a pretty gold ribbon and hands it off to Phainon, wishing him luck with wooing whatever lucky lady the candies are for. Phainon can't help the way his cheeks redden at that, because he most certainly is not trying to woo Mydei with sweets, but he decides against correcting the man, simply thanking him with a smile before quickly heading out of the markets and towards the clinic.

I'm coming, Mydei, and I'm not letting you weasel your way out of telling the truth this time.

Chapter End Notes

I promise they're gonna fuck nasty soon. Anyway, thank you to every single one of you who've commented, subscribed, bookmarked, left kudos, etc. I appreciate you all so much!

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Just Call My Name, I'm Yours to Tame
chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

OH MY GOOOOOOOOOD this chapter took FOREVER to write and it's HUGE!!! I got a little carried away, but I really hope you guys enjoy the final build up before smut city. Sorry not sorry for how much talking happens in this chapter, but there's juicy bits as well, so I hope you find it interesting! Once again thank you all for your kind words! I really appreciate each and every one of you that's left a kudos, a comment, or even just continued to check back for updates to the story! Thanks so much!

Mydei has never experienced the feeling of waking up in a hospital setting before, and it's all too strange when he finally cracks his eyes open to see a white marble ceiling above him, harsh daylight streaming in through the window of the exam room and making him wince from the sudden brightness. It's a slow process waking up from his blacked-out state, and he groans as he finally starts to feel the effects that overheating to the point of fainting has had on his body. His head is throbbing and his limbs feel heavy, and he feels the strange sensation of something cold flowing into the veins of his arm. That’s certainly enough to alert him that he is not in his home, not in his own bed, and it startles him into sitting up, eyes darting around the room to take in the foreign surroundings.

Oh. This is Hyacine's clinic.

He recognizes it despite having only been here once or twice before to be patched up after a particularly rough battle, even if he'd protested coming every time. He’s just fine with field medics sewing up his wounds in tattered tents, or simply not having anyone tend to them at all, because his body will heal quickly enough on its own, and he'd rather not occupy the healer's time when there's no danger of him dying from his injuries. Not permanently, anyway. This time, however, there's no pain, and he's incredibly confused as to why he's here, because one glance over his body is enough to tell him that he has no external injuries, so why…?

He tries to recall what had transpired that might have led to him being hospitalized, but his brain just feels so foggy, and these unfamiliar surroundings are downright disorienting. He also notices that he's been stripped of his armor, leaving only his pants and chiton on, something that makes him feel uncomfortably vulnerable. It has him wanting to get up and leave as soon as possible, but the moment he shifts on the bed he feels a tug at his arm, and when he glances down he sees a thin, clear tube sticking out of a taped-up spot near the crook of his elbow.

Ah. He's hooked up to an IV for some reason. The sight of it has him frowning deeply, and he instinctively goes to pull the foreign object out of his arm, but as soon as he tries it a round ball of fluff proceeds to fly into the room and invade his personal space, bumping into his free arm none too gently to tell him to cut it the hell out. Mydei huffs in indignation as Little Ica doots at him, finally letting go of the tubing when the tiny pegasus refuses to quit jostling his arm to stop him from pulling it out.

"Alright, alright. Clearly you know best," he grumbles, giving up for now, and right on cue Hyacine comes running into the room, a little out of breath but still as bright and bubbly as ever. When she sees that Mydei is awake she breathes a sigh of relief, approaching his bed with a warm little smile.

"You're awake! As soon as I heard all the fussing Ica was doing I knew something had to be up. How are you feeling, Lord Mydei?" Hyacine asks, already starting the process of checking all his vitals again, as diligent as ever. Mydei is still incredibly confused about why he's even here, but allows Hyacine to do her job, if only to get her to stop fussing over him.

"I'm fine. My head is throbbing and my mind feels fuzzy, but it's hardly anything to be concerned about," he insists, even if that doesn't stop Hyacine from checking his pulse and jotting down the numbers on a notepad she'd pulled from her pocket. She hums, reaching up to feel his forehead and frowning a little.

"The headache is to be expected, as well as the brain fog. Your temperature is still elevated though…perhaps due to your pre-heat," she states, and the mere mention of that has Mydei grumbling even more. Right. His pre-heat. Because the gods apparently weren't content with the suffering he's endured in his life so far, so of course they saw fit to inflict such a thing upon him.

"Right. More importantly, why am I here? The last thing I remember is being in the baths-" he abruptly cuts himself off when the memories suddenly come flooding back into his mind, and oh yeah, his idiotic competition with Phainon…that must've been what landed him here, even if he has no idea how. Good thing Hyacine is here to fill in the gaps, even if the look she gives him is none too pleased.

"You fainted in the baths due to the extremely high temperature of the water combined with your already elevated body temperature from your pre-heat. I've already scolded Lord Phainon for it, even if I'm glad that he brought you straight here when it happened," she says with a weary sigh, finally tucking her notepad back into her pocket and crossing her arms over her chest like a disappointed parent. Mydei at least has the decency to look guilty as she scolds him, though the revelation that it was Phainon who brought him here makes him feel both annoyed and flustered in equal measure. "I also left your damp clothes on in an effort to help lower your body temperature faster, so I apologize if you feel uncomfortable in them."

Uncomfortable is an understatement, but it's nothing he can't endure. What bothers him more is being confined to a hospital bed, but something tells him that Hyacine isn't going to let him get up just yet.

"How humiliating…being carried here by the Deliverer because my body couldn't take the heat is hardly befitting of a crown prince of Kremnos," he mumbles, his pride thoroughly bruised from the whole ordeal, but some small part of him feels just a tiny bit touched that the alpha had taken care of him without a second thought. Not that he'd ever admit that out loud, of course. He pointedly avoids Hyacine's gaze, instead turning his attention towards Little Ica, who's decided that his lap is the place to be, his chubby little body surprisingly light despite how hefty it looks. Mydei can't help but pet the little guy, the pegasus's white coat feeling surprisingly soft, almost like how Mydei imagines a cloud would feel. The attention earns him a pleased little doot from Ica, and Hyacine can't help but smile at the sight.

"Don't worry, Lord Mydei. Even if others might have seen you being carried here by Lord Phainon you can always say it's because you were wounded in battle," Hyacine suggests, and while it doesn't really make him feel any better he appreciates the gesture nonetheless.

"Right. Where is that fool, anyway?" he asks, hoping that Phainon hasn't landed himself in the hospital as well, even if that would even the score. Hyacine finally finishes her exam and proceeds to plop down on the edge of the bed, and only now does Mydei realize just how worn out she looks. A pang of guilt wells up inside him at the sight, but at least she seems to be in good spirits, he supposes.

"I ordered him to go change out of his wet clothes and eat something because he was too busy worrying about you to care for himself," she says, and while Mydei isn't surprised in the slightest to learn that Phainon had once again neglected his own well-being to look after someone else instead he can't help but want to throttle him for it anyway. The thought has him sighing heavily, because he feels directly responsible for the state that he and Phainon both ended up in.

"I shouldn't have taken him up on his offer to spar, but if I hadn't he would have figured out that something is wrong with me," he says a bit defensively, and now it's Hyacine's turn to sigh, because as much as she adores her friends they can be real idiots sometimes.

"Lord Mydei, I really think you should just be honest with him about your condition. He's already tried to get answers from me about it, but I refused to tell him because I didn't want to violate your right to privacy concerning your medical history. However, I've never seen Lord Phainon so worried, and hiding the truth from him is only going to make things worse." Hyacine may not be a therapist in name, but her words of wisdom do indeed resonate with Mydei, even if telling Phainon the truth is bound to open up a whole new can of worms for him to deal with. Still, Mydei is tired of running from the truth, tired of having to make up excuses that he's almost certain that Phainon is too clever to buy, and so he finally decides to give in and confess…once Phainon returns, anyway.

"…alright, fine. I'll tell him, even if I already know what he's going to say," Mydei grumbles, fingers brushing through Ica's soft, fluffy mane in an attempt to soothe the simmering doubt and uncertainty in his gut. Hyacine nods in approval, smiling at him, even if she looks completely exhausted now.

"I'm sure he'll be willing to listen to whatever you have to say, Lord Mydei," Hyacine's words are muffled by a yawn mid-sentence, causing Mydei to eye her with a critical expression.

"Let's hope so. You, meanwhile, should get some rest. You look like you're about to fall asleep sitting up," he says with a hint of amusement in his voice. Hyacine blinks blearily before rubbing at her eyes, and Little Ica lets out a doot of agreement, waddling over to plop down in his master's lap instead. She smiles tiredly down at the little pegasus, giving him a scritch behind the ears.

"Normally I'd argue that I'm fine, but…the truth is that I haven't had the chance to rest much since yesterday. Not that I mind helping friends, of course! It's just that I'm afraid I might make mistakes when I'm this exhausted, so I might take your advice and try to squeeze in a nap before more patients show up."

Mydei is glad that at least one among their group of friends is willing to listen to reason, because he'd never forgive himself if Hyacine also ended up passing out in her own clinic. "Good. Before you go though, can you take this out?" he gestures to the IV sticking out of his arm, and Hyacine looks hesitant for a moment before nodding and moving to start unwrapping the bandage securing the IV in Mydei's arm.

"Alright. I think you're well enough not to need it anymore. Promise me you'll drink plenty of water once you leave though. Ah, speaking of leaving, I suppose if you're feeling better I can't justify keeping you here, but Lord Phainon should be returning soon, and he might panic if your hospital bed is empty when he gets back," she says, fighting back another yawn as she pulls the tubing out of Mydei's arm, a few droplets of golden blood escaping before she wraps his arm up securely with a fresh bandage. He nods in agreement to her conditions, even if he doesn't particularly want to spend his evening chugging water.

"Fine." That's all he has to say about it, really.

Once she's finished she throws the tubing away and has Mydei flex his arm a couple of times to ensure that the bandage will stay in place, and with that she's finally ready to discharge him officially. She has him sign some sort of paper and then he's free to go, but he promises to stay until Phainon returns, not wanting to cause the alpha any more distress.

And, as if on cue, the second Hyacine turns to leave Phainon enters the room, looking a bit out of breath but otherwise perfectly fine. His scent hits Mydei almost immediately, and he fights back a blush as he shifts on the bed, moving to sit on the edge of it to make room for the alpha, just in case he wants to sit with him or something. Not that Mydei wants him to or anything.

Phainon's eyes go wide when he sees Mydei up and awake, the look of shock quickly followed by one of relief as he rushes over to the bed, and if he had a tail it would no doubt be wagging a mile a minute.

"Mydei, you're awake! Thank the titans" he exclaims, and Mydei crosses his arms over his chest with a huff, trying and failing not to look happy to see the man.

"More like thank Hyacine," he nods towards said girl, who's currently watching the two of them with a knowing little smile that makes Mydei want to shove his face into a pillow and yell. Phainon beams at her, and Mydei wonders if it's possible for one tiny room to contain this amount of sunshine and rainbows.

"Yeah! Thank you, Hyacine, you're the best. I really owe you one," Phainon sounds like he's ready to pledge his eternal service to Hyacine out of sheer gratefulness, but she simply shakes her head with a tiny laugh, ever the humble one.

"No need to thank me, Lord Phainon. I just did what any doctor would do," she says, hands behind her back as she rocks on her heels. "I've officially discharged Lord Mydei, so he can leave when he feels up to it. However, I'd like to ask you to keep an eye on him for a while and make sure he doesn't do anything else reckless," she says with a wink, only half-teasing, and Mydei grumbles under his breath, because he most certainly does not need a babysitter, thank you very much.

Phainon chuckles, giving her a nod. "Got it. I'll take it from here, Hyacine, don't worry. Now go get some rest, you look beat!"

For once Hyacine doesn't argue, nodding in agreement before instructing the two of them to come wake her up from her nap in one of the small resting rooms reserved for staff should they need anything. With that she departs, and of course Little Ica follows his human, fluttering after her as she exits the room. And then they're left alone, something that normally wouldn't faze Mydei, but given everything that's transpired he can't help but feel just the slightest bit anxious about the conversation he knows is coming. At least Phainon isn't interrogating him just yet, instead coming to sit next to him on the bed, and it's then that Mydei notices the small box in his hands, eyeing it curiously.

"What's that?" he asks, pointing to the gold-trimmed box, and the little blush that appears on Phainon's cheeks just then makes Mydei want to tackle him onto the bed and-

No. No, none of that. That's dangerous thinking right there. Stupid hormones…

"Oh, um, this is actually a gift…for you," Phainon says bashfully, which is new, but Mydei can't say he dislikes it. A gift for him, though? He's not exactly sure what he did to earn such a thing, but he can't stop the way his own cheeks light up at the news, his traitorous heart beating just a little bit faster now.

"For me? Why?" he asks, trying and failing to hide how flustered he is as Phainon hands the decorative box over to him. They must look like a couple of teenagers on their very first date, but at least nobody else is around to see them. He carefully unties the decorative ribbon before lifting the lid off the box, revealing a plethora of delectable looking candies of all sorts inside. His eyes go wide with both surprise and delight at the sight, and Phainon beams brighter than Kephale's Dawn Device when he sees the positive reaction to his gift.

"Because I thought that ingesting some sugar might help boost your energy back up. And also because I wanted to," Phainon says softly, and Mydei quickly decides to pick up a piece of the candy and shove it in his mouth to distract himself from how ridiculously adorable the alpha is being right now. It's a piece of candied pomegranate, featuring a crunchy, sugary shell surrounding a cluster of soft, tart arils that make Mydei's taste buds sing in delight as they burst on his tongue. His face lights up as he savors the candy, and the way Phainon's scent slowly shifts to something warm and summery as he watches him, all sea breezes and citrus, doesn't escape Mydei’s notice.

"I take it you like them?" Phainon asks with amusement, and Mydei huffs as he goes in for another piece, this one some kind of hard candy tasting of honey and lavender. He takes a moment to crunch it up and swallow it before glancing up from the box again to see a very excited looking Phainon staring at him intently, as if awaiting his opinion with bated breath. Kephale preserve him…

"Not bad. It seems you have taste after all," he says teasingly, the little quirk of his lips upward clearly indicating that yes, he is indeed pleased with the gift. But…he supposes it won't hurt to actually voice his gratitude for once. "…thanks."

"Yeah, of course!" Phainon looks about ready to explode from the praise, his scent so overwhelmingly wonderful now that Mydei feels his traitorous body reacting to it already, slicking up in a way that makes him want to jump right out the nearest window. At least his pants are still slightly damp from the bath, so even if it were to soak through his underwear he could just blame it on that. It doesn't help that his instincts are insisting that this gift is some kind of courting behavior, when Mydei is almost certain that it's just Phainon being Phainon. He'd probably gift any one of his friends something like this if they were sick or injured, even if the thought makes Mydei feel weirdly jealous for some stupid reason.

It's just hormones is all.

There's a brief moment of peaceful silence between them as Mydei eats a few more pieces of candy, the sugar doing wonders to help give him a little burst of energy just like Phainon had hoped. It's enough for him to be able to make it home without needing to stop to rest, at least. It really is a thoughtful gift, and if Mydei's scent were detectable right now he'd no doubt smell like honey and pomegranate from how pleased he is, sweet and enticing. He does wonder if Phainon is going to ask about his lack of a scent again, but he'd also rather not spoil the moment, so he won't bring it up unless the alpha does first.

However when Phainon breaks the silence it isn't with a question, the alpha sobering up a little as he gives Mydei an apologetic look. "I…also might have bought the candies as a sort of apology, because I feel responsible for what happened," he admits, suddenly looking sheepish, and Mydei blinks, clearly confused. He can't figure out for the life of him why Phainon would be blaming himself for him fainting in the baths, as if he'd dragged Mydei there by force or something.

"What? Why?"

Phainon's scent dampens a little, like a summer rain. "Because I suggested that we go to the bathhouse instead of insisting that you take it easy after you said you were feeling a little under the weather. Even if you probably would've insisted that you were fine I still should have told you to rest," he says, deflating like a kicked puppy, but this time the only one kicking Phainon is himself. Mydei simply stares at him for a moment before letting out an exasperated sigh, setting the candies aside for now.

"Enough. I went with you willingly, and I refuse to place the blame solely on you when it was I who insisted we have that idiotic contest in the first place," he says with a hint of annoyance in his voice, though this time it's aimed solely towards himself. He really has been acting like an idiot lately, but at least he realizes that now, even if it's not the easiest thing to admit out loud. Phainon shakes his head though, obviously not entirely convinced that Mydei's current condition isn't somehow his fault, the moron.

"But-"

"I said enough, Deliverer. I have no idea why you're always so eager to throw yourself on the pyre, but the blame is not yours to bear this time," he says firmly, leaving no room for any doubts or questioning, and thankfully Phainon gets the hint, even if he visibly winces at the call-out. Mydei's inner omega very much dislikes that he's said such harsh words to the alpha, but he's also pointedly ignoring it, because he's not going to simply sit back and let Phainon blame himself for every little thing that goes wrong in their lives.

"Alright, alright. I'll let you take the blame this time, I suppose." Phainon agreeing with him has Mydei relaxing a little again, and when the alpha reaches over him to snatch one of the candies from the box he allows it, this time. Watching his face light up as he crunches into the candy is quite a treat in itself, after all. "Oh wow, these really are good! I'll have to thank the vendor the next time I pass by his stall," he says, licking his lips clean of any lingering sugary sweetness, and Mydei pointedly ignores the stirring of arousal inside him at the sight of that cute, pink tongue.

Kephale above, pull yourself together.

Phainon thankfully doesn't try pilfering any more of his sweets, instead leaning back on his hands and looking thoughtful for a moment. Mydei can already guess what he's thinking about, even if part of him had hoped that he'd be able to escape the conversation he's been dreading all this time. What a fool he is.

"I know now might not be the best time to bring this up, but…I've been worried about you all day, Mydei. First there was your scent being non-existent, and then you being hesitant to spar, and then you passing out in the baths…something is clearly wrong, especially when I've never seen you have any trouble tolerating heat," Phainon says, brows furrowing as he looks at Mydei imploringly. It's enough to have that nasty guilty feeling welling up inside Mydei all over again, his appetite suddenly vanishing completely. He lets Phainon speak though, because he owes him at least that much.
